correctness.rationale: Unitary Fourier analysis pairs k and k+N/2 under alternate-vertex restriction, giving orthogonal blocks Q_δ=1/sqrt2[[1,1],[e^{-(2-δ)t},e^{-(2+δ)t}]], δ=2|cos(2πk/N)|; no hidden normalization factor appears for counting-measure norms. The Gram trace and determinant for sqrt2 Q are T=2+2q cosh(2δt), D=2q(cosh(2δt)-1), q=e^{-4t}, and T′=D′>0. Their eigenvalues straddle 1, so both branches grow with δ; min δ=0 iff 4|N, otherwise 2sin(π/N), while max δ=2. The resulting exact A_N and B_N follow by quadratic roots. A_N/d_N²→h(t)=t²/(1+e^{4t}) compact-uniformly, and Rayleigh upper envelope A_N/d_N²<=t²e^{-2t} excludes maximizers at t→0 or infinity. The unique positive maximizer solves 2τ=1+e^{-4τ}, and N d_N→2π gives the constant. Independently rebuilt full complex cycle heat matrices for N=4..20 (even) and five t values, verifying 45 exact Gram extrema within 2e-12. Universal and limit assertions rely on proof not tests.
